subject: MAP milestone: traffic-replay & load test — draft schedule and sizing
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Burns <eburns@saasco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP milestone: traffic-replay & load test — draft schedule and sizing

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is a one-page draft MAP milestone for the performance/load validation step we discussed. Quick recap and asks so we can lock dates: 

Summary from today's discovery:
- Objective: run a traffic-replay load test to validate tail latency and throughput under peak QPS (production-like traffic) before committing Dedicated capacity.
- Target metrics: sustained 90th/95th token latency targets and <1% error rate at peak load.
- Window preferences: you said weekends are preferable; engineering embargo on 2/26–2/28.

Proposed draft milestone (see attached map_milestone_draft_v1.xlsx):
- Test window (candidate): Sat 2027-03-06 02:00–08:00 PT (6h test with 30m ramp up/down)
- Responsible: Redwood SE (Karthik Iyer) to run and monitor; SaaSCo to provide traffic replay file and verification users (Emily / platform-eng).
- Dedicated capacity recommendation: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (quantized model build) to meet projected peak QPS ~7,200 reqs/sec (estimated from your 30M daily sessions). Karthik will confirm sizing after a quick profiler run.
- Dependencies before test:
  - SaaSCo to deliver anonymized traffic_profile_v3.json at least 72 hours prior
  - Exchange of KMS key info for telemetry (if needed)
  - Confirm SLO rollback policy and canary fallback model versions

Next steps / asks from you:
1) Confirm the candidate window (Mar 6) or propose two alternate weekend windows.
2) Share the traffic_profile_v3.json and any synthetic user auth tokens we should use for replay.
3) Any compliance constraints (e.g., data anonymization checklist) we should follow for logs.

I copied Marissa to keep CS looped for post-test remediation and support. Karthik will jump in on sizing and runbook.

Attachments: map_milestone_draft_v1.xlsx, saasco_traffic_profile_v3.json, rdw_test_plan_brief.pdf

Thanks —
Rafael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rah@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: MAP milestone: traffic-replay & load test — draft schedule and sizing

Rafael —

Thanks for the clear recap and the draft MAP. A few items from our side: 

1) Window: Mar 6 works for us as a first option. Our SREs asked whether we can start 03:00–09:00 PT instead (shift +1h) because of an internal backup job that runs at 01:30. If you can accommodate that shift, we’ll lock it.

2) Traffic file: we can provide an anonymized traffic_profile_v3.json by Tue 2027-03-02. It will remove PII and replace user IDs with stable hashed IDs. Platform-eng will also include a short mapping doc for the replay tokens.

3) Compliance question: we need confirmation on log retention and where telemetry will be stored. Are you able to provide SOC2 artifacts and outline what telemetry is uploaded to Redwood? We’ll need to include that in the procurement packet.

4) Capacity: the 8x A100 suggestion sounds reasonable, but our platform team prefers you to run a small profiler run first to validate that number. Karthik — can you confirm the profiler duration & what artifacts you need from us?

We are CCing platform-eng to coordinate the technical handoff.

Emily Burns
Director, Platform Engineering | SaaSCo
eburns@saasco.com | +1 (212) 555-8842

Hi all —

Quick technical reply from the SE side (thanks for the context, Emily). I reviewed the attached traffic profile and have a few notes & asks before I sign off on the 8x A100 estimate: 

Profiler run plan (what I need):
- Short profiler: 30–45 minutes against a small subset (10% of your replay) to capture sequence length distribution, tokenization distribution, and avg tokens per request. Please give us a 1GB gzipped sample of the traffic file (anonymized) — not the full set.
- Expected deliverable: a profiler report (I produce) within 8 business hours of the run. This will either confirm 8x A100 or move us to a 6x or 10x target depending on KV cache hit rates and peak sequence lengths.

Runbook items (for the actual weekend test):
- 30m gradual ramp (10% -> 100%), 4h steady-state, 30m ramp down.
- Health checks: token error rate, 95th latency, GPU memory telemetry, and model OOM counters.
- Fallback: immediate rollback to a smaller model variant and auto-throttle if error rate >1.0% for 3 consecutive minutes.

Telemetry & data handling:
- We keep ephemeral logs on the test cluster for 7 days by default and can provide an export (S3 presigned URL) for you post-test. We do not store PII — logs are sanitized at ingestion as long as the sample file is anonymized as you described. For SOC2 artifacts: Rafael / Marissa can share our compliance pack (SOC2 Type II summary & data handling statement) via the Drive link earlier.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Emily: drop a 1GB gzipped sample to the Drive folder or share a presigned link by Mon 2027-03-01.
2) I’ll run the profiler on Tue 2027-03-02 or Wed 2027-03-03 (depending on when sample arrives).
3) Confirm final test window after profiler results — but tentatively hold Mar 6 03:00–09:00 PT as requested.

Happy to jump on a 20-min tech sync if anyone wants to walk the replay format.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
k.iyer@redwood.ai
